The document under this number does not correspond to the text because the document speaks about something entirely different, whereas the documents 65 ter 1D02690 and 1D02733 would be the appropriate numbers that would reflect what the witness stated in paragraph 53 of his statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, if I may just get clarification. Which of these two, 1D02690 and 1D02733, would support this paragraph and replace 1D13031, or do they both do the same?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Both, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is not possible, Mr. Stojanovic. One document mentioned with the number of the Karadzic case can't be two documents in our case; this is not possible. And the confusion is -- I think Mr. Traldi was referring to, is you have different numbers mentioned in the attachment to your 92 ter motion and in the Defence exhibit list we received some days ago. So there are two numbers. Please clarify which one is exactly that one the witness speaks about in paragraph 53.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, 1D02690.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Do we then understand, Mr. Stojanovic, that 1D02690 is to replace 1D13031?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And in addition, can -- in addition to that, can you please state the title of the document? Is it the RS MUP CSB Romansko [phoen] Information or is it the SDA Executive Committee?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, that is the document of the Executive Board of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is -- it should be 1D02690.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's the one to replace 1D13031. Okay. Then where does 1D02733 fit in in the testimony of this witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a document accompanying the basic document, and it supports and spells out in more concrete terms the communication from the Executive Board of the SDA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Then it is not an associated exhibit with this explanation?

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, it is my understanding during the Karadzic case these two documents were joined as one exhibit, as is often the case in these trials, and that that is why they are two documents in ours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I understand that. I understand that practice in this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. IVETIC
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, with the last witness we had documents that were joined together yesterday that were multiple documents in one exhibit number that were admitted by this Chamber, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But they are --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Could I -- could I suggest -- we are not in combat. When one counsel stands up, could the other sit down. Yes, Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The problem is that you confused the numbers in the list that you have provided the Chamber with, and we just want to know where the numbers appear under which title in which paragraph of the statement; otherwise, we can't admit them as associated exhibits.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So, Your Honours, in the document that we submitted to you as associated exhibits for the statement of this witness, we said that for paragraph 53 we are going to use these two documents as associated exhibits. According to 65 ter, they have the numbers that we have already referred to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are you saying the SDA archive reports deal with what you would call in paragraph 53 the policy of the SDA?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. According to the information I have, in the Karadzic case it was one document and we informed you in writing on the 22nd of September.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I would suggest to -- to save time and to clarify the situation that you show both documents by asking the witness in relation to the content of paragraph 53, and then we can admit them as associated exhibits or as separate documents. We don't know how they are uploaded and the problem, again, is the confusion created by the two lists. Therefore --

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. That's what we are going to do. Could we please have 1D2690 in e-court -- 1D02690.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you have a document before you?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: My question: Have you had an opportunity to see this document earlier on and does this document refer to what you testified about in paragraph 53?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I've seen this before and it has to do with the training of policemen in other areas. It's a document sent by the SDA.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We didn't receive interpretation.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Can you hear the English booth now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please have another document in e-court, 1D02733.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, could you please tell the Court what this document says?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: It says how trainee policemen are to be admitted in the training centre of the MUP of the Republic of Croatia.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Does this document say who it is that is sending MUP employees of Bosnia-Herzegovina to be trained in the MUP of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: SDA headquarters.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us whether one can see on the basis of this document what the name of candidate is, the candidate who was sent?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We no longer hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Witness, the interpreters can't hear you. Could you please try to speak closer to the mike without coming too close. But if you stand away from it, then we don't hear. Can you repeat your question?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can see the first name, it is Mirsad, but the last name is illegible.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Is that a Muslim name?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Where do we find that in the English, Mr. Stojanovic? I see something written in the English handwritten question -- question mark Fadil Polic, and then slash -- forward slash.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. This name that you have before you is, I think, the third page of the document in B/C/S because now these are several documents sending several different persons. So in B/C/S could we please take a look at this document -- or rather, its third page. I apologise, the second page. The second page. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, can you see the name of the candidate that is being sent for training to the MUP of the Republic of Croatia?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: It's so dark. I cannot discern it.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we zoom in on this darker area where there is a handwritten note.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Can you read it now?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Sadik, roughly, that's the first name; and the last name is illegible again. No, it's Fadil maybe.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I -- now, Mr. Stojanovic, obviously this document is more than one page. How many pages is it? Now we're going to tender all these names?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And how many pages is this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document consists of -- I just need a moment. 40 pages, Your Honour, with different names of persons who are enrolled in the course.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Now paragraph 53 is talking about policy. You now want to give 40 pages of individual recommendations which are repeating the same fact. Would one not be sufficient as a demonstration of that policy?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think so, Your Honour, if there is no dispute between us that all of these persons are ethnic Muslims.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We will come to that. You can verify that with the opposite counsel. And the other document, 1D02690, was it a one-pager or was it also several pages?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one page, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Traldi --

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Ah.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: -- does this resolve your problems?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, no objections to 65 ter 1D02690 and we're happy to speak to the Defence. I admit off the top of my head, I'm unable to speak to the ethnicity of the names.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Is that okay by you? Okay, so we defer the admission of that 02733 until you have spoken.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That would be my proposal, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you so much. Mr. Registrar, 1D02341 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D733, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. And 1D02690 is also admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit D734, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Stojanovic, I notice it's time for a break. Would that be a convenient time?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. After the break, I don't think I'll need more than ten minutes or so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: One observation, Mr. Stojanovic. The last document we now have admitted into evidence was not listed as an associated exhibit in your 92 ter motion. I just want to clarify that. This created the problem.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You're right, Your Honour. And that is why on the 22nd of September we submitted a document stating that we would be using this document as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And just to round off this topic, is it correct that then D733 and D734 replace in paragraph 53 of the witness's statement 1D13031?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Mr. Registrar, to the extent that it affects your department, can you attend to that.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. That will be noted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Yes, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Just for the record, I think 1D13031 is the Karadzic case number which was used --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: -- and 1D02343 is the Mladic case number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Then it has fallen out of our case now. It's no longer part of our case. Mr. Djuric, we are going to take a short break of 20 minutes and we would like to see you back here in 20 minutes' time. You can follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I see you are on your feet, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I'd mentioned I had one issue to raise in private session, and I wonder if now might be a convenient moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It will be. May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. We will take a break of 20 minutes. We'll come back at 25 minutes past. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the witness please be escorted into the courtroom. Mr. Stojanovic, you said you still have ten minutes?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is the plan. Your Honour, I intend to read the summary and then put just a few short questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I would like to read this witness's statement's summary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness Mane Djuric holds a master's degree in mechanical engineer. Before the war, he was a republican inspector for fire protection at the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia and Herzegovina in the security services centre in Tuzla. His office was in the Vlasenica public security station. He knows why the Crisis Staff was established in Vlasenica; he is aware of the reasons and motives. He says that the tasks of the Crisis Staff were to monitor the situation and take measures in order to overcome all the crisis situations in the municipality; however, the Crisis Staff was short-lived due to the dissipation of its membership, and finally a decision was taken to divide the municipality of Vlasenica into three different parts: A Muslim part, a Serbian part, and a separate municipality of Milici. He also speaks about what he knows about the arming of both Serbs and Muslims, about the reasons why Muslims were leaving Vlasenica. He says that the process took place in three different stages and he puts things in a chronological perspective. He says that the main reason for the departure of Serbs and Muslims from Vlasenica was security, fear of revenges and retaliation because of the forcible eviction of Serbs from their houses in other cities. He is aware of all the efforts to disarm people who had illegal weapons. He knows about paramilitary formations which existed in Vlasenica, and he's aware of the situation of the judiciary in Vlasenica municipality. As for the Susica facility, he claims that it was originally set up as a reception centre to accommodate all those who needed safe accommodation irrespective of their ethnic affiliation. People stayed there for a very short period of time until the moment a transport was made available to them to take them where they wanted to go. At first the centre was secured by the Territorial Defence, and later by the VRS. People would stay there only a couple of days and then they would leave. He also knows that there were activities aimed at moving Muslims from the Susica reception centre to Bijeljina. And finally, the witness speaks about what he knows about the setting up of a Muslim paramilitary formations back in 1991. Their names were the Patriotic League and the Green Berets. He also speaks about the role of the political leadership in the setting up and training of those units. This is a short summary of this witness's statement. With your leave, Your Honours, I would like to put a couple of questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You may proceed, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Sir, just something about your CV. When did you become the deputy chief of the public security station in Zvornik?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: In April 1994. I believe that that was sometime around the 27th or the 28th of April.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to call up D732 in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: It's your statement. I'm interested in paragraph 21 -- 29. In paragraph 29 in the sentence you say that you thought it would be possible to discipline the unit in question, and then you say that Commander Radenko Stanic and you invited the commander of that intervention platoon, Miroslav Kraljevic, and his deputy, Elvis Djuric, to a meeting and that you agreed that they would continue working in the police in a certain way. To your best recollection, when was that? When were those units included into the police in Vlasenica in that way?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Just by way of introduction, that intervention platoon existed as a unit of the Territorial Defence by establishment; however, on the 12th of May a decision was taken to set up the Army Republika Srpska. Later on there was a general mobilisation proclaimed by the Serbian -- by the Muslim Presidency of Bosnia-Herzegovina and that was the beginning of 1992. A decision was taken that all the units had to be under the command of the Republika Srpska --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, sorry. Can I interrupt you, Mr. Djuric. You are talking a little too fast. The interpreters can't keep pace with you. Could you slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you. A decision was taken that all militarily able-bodied men had to be under the command of the Army of Republika Srpska or the Territorial Defence or the MUP of Republika Srpska. That unit was part of the TO. At that moment it did not want to join the Army of Republika Srpska. So the Crisis Staff and the leadership decided to attach that unit to the MUP, i.e., to the public security station, which was a legal institution at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: The question -- let me interrupt you for a moment because we can see that in your written statement. Can you remember the date when that happened?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: That happened sometime between the 10th and the 15th or 16th of June, 1992. They were finally attached to the public security station in a formal way.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. And now let's look at paragraph 35 in your statement.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, this is D732 again. I believe that I will use the following page in the English version because I'm interested in the very last sentence in paragraph 35 and that's on the following English page -- English version. I would kindly ask that the following page be displayed in the English version. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: You say that people were leaving, both Serbs and Muslims, the territory of the municipality of Vlasenica. You speak about the procedure and you end up by saying: "I suppose this was done because of the International Red Cross so that it could be demonstrated that no one left under duress." Could you please tell the Trial Chamber why did you suppose that that was done on account of the International Committee of the Red Cross?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: In the previous period we said that both Serbs and Muslims were leaving; however, the intensity of these departures went up and down depending on the security situation over there in the area and in the surrounding area. There were some periods of time when the departures became more intensive and then it also worked the other way around. As for these departures, the Red Cross was informed so that for these groups of people who were leaving - primarily Muslims going towards Kladanj and Tuzla - proper accommodation should be found for them there and the International Red Cross was informed about that, too. As for constant pressures, namely that somebody is forcing somebody out of Vlasenica, then probably it was the assessment of the Crisis Staff that a procedure should be adopted for those who wished to leave the municipality of Vlasenica, that they should sign a paper stating that their departure was voluntary. That pertained to Muslims. And at that moment for the Serbs that meant that -- I mean, there should be control over military conscripts as to who had left the territory and who had not. So my personal opinion is that this decision of the Crisis Staff is the result of a compromise with the International Red Cross to show that no one was leaving under duress; rather, people were doing that of their own free will.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: I'm just going to end with a concrete question: From whom did you receive this information that this was done because the Red Cross had asked for that?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: The representatives of the International Red Cross often stopped by the public security station, and they kept raising this question regarding the departure of these citizens. So among others the representatives of the International Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Djuric. Could you please just speak a bit more slowly when you answer the questions that are put to you by my colleague, the Prosecutor. We need to do that for the record.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honours. I have no further questions at this point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Stojanovic. Yes, Mr. Traldi. Mr. Djuric, you are now going to be cross-examined by Mr. Traldi. Mr. Traldi is counsel for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And thanks to Mr. Stojanovic as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Good afternoon, sir.

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you've been interviewed by the Office of the Prosecutor of this Tribunal twice; correct?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you told the truth on those occasions; correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Yes, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, I'm going to briefly now go through your positions during the relevant period. Before the war, you were a fire inspector under the authority of CSB Tuzla; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In April 1992 you were mobilised into the police force of SJB Vlasenica?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: From April to August 1992 you were acting chief of SJB Vlasenica; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, but intensively from about the 20th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: Could the witness please be asked to speak into the microphone. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, sir, you're being asked just to speak towards the microphone to assist the interpreters and keeping the record clear. We'd agreed that from April to August you'd served as acting chief of SJB. In August 1992 you were formally appointed as chief by Zoran Cvijetic; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. In April until the 20th of May it was Rade Bjelanovic who was acting chief, and then he went to the public security station in Milici. From the 20th of May until August, we can say that I was acting chief. And from the 8th of August, 1992, I was appointed by the minister as chief of the public security station.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you were appointed by Mr. Cvijetic. He was the head of the CSB Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And SJB Vlasenica was under the authority of the CSB Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, from April it was under CSB Sarajevo and up until then, that is to say while the MUP of the former BH existed, it was within the CSB Tuzla.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So from April it was under the CSB Sarajevo as part of the Republika Srpska MUP; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: That's right. The MUP of the Serb Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. That's what it was called at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: That's right. It would have become the Republika Srpska MUP later in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Later, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now approximately every month you yourself would attend collegiums held by Mr. Cvijetic; right? The man who appointed you.

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Well, it can be put that way. That is to say, collegium meetings were held once a month, but if necessary even more frequently than that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And those were held sometimes in the CSB headquarters in Lukavica?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And sometimes at the Hotel Kosuta in Pale?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can you briefly describe the purpose of such meetings?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: The purpose of these meetings - if we can call them the collegium of the chief of CSB - was to provide information about the situation in areas of different public security stations, another thing that was very important there. What was discussed was the constitution and the mode of functioning of these stations because the newly created situation was such, especially where SJB Vlasenica was, that was beforehand within the CSB of Tuzla and now it became part of the CSB Sarajevo. It had to do with the way in which communication and co-ordination, everything else, was to be established, all other links within that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And Mr. Cvijetic would report on these meetings, these collegiums, and what he had heard there to Minister Stanisic; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: At any rate, it was his duty to convey information to the minister -- or rather, the minister's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: His immediate superior, was that Minister Stanisic or Under-Secretary Cedo Kljaic?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Mico Stanisic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now in November 1993 while you were SJB chief, you were proposed for a decoration by Mr. Cvijetic; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Can the Prosecution have 65 ter 31514.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, this is a document labelled "Submission of Proposals for Decoration," coming from Mr. Cvijetic and dated the 10th of November, 1993. He was still your direct superior at this time; correct?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could turn to page 2 in both the English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We'll see your name at point 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And then if we could turn to page 5 in the English and 4 in the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We see you're being proposed for a decoration of the second rank and a description of the reasons. And it says here - I'm looking at the second sentence: "Immediately after war operations began, he was named and appointed Vlasenica SJB chief, at which time he undertook practical steps in establishment and organisation - work in the SJB. He timely carried out organisational preparations for Vlasenica SJB to be put into function for the Serb people's liberation." Those are activities you'd reported to Mr. Cvijetic through the line of work that you had carried out; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: In your view, when did war operations begin in Vlasenica municipality?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: We can say the following: As for some date, the 21st of April, 1992, it meant the realisation of many decisions reached by the Crisis Staff; inter alia, there was a decision on disarming the reserve force and the active duty policemen, and also taking away illegal weapons, the decision on establishing the TO, the decision on declaring an imminent threat of war, and perhaps some other decisions. I cannot remember exactly. So some period where more active efforts were being made in organising the defence, that would be the 21st of April, 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you received two decorations in November 1993; right? The order of Milos Obilic was one of them?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'd tender this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6869, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: You mentioned during direct examination that on 27 April 1994 you'd become deputy chief of the new securities services centre in Zvornik. This was effectively a promotion; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Viewed in terms of hierarchy and the establishment of the Ministry of the Interior, yes, it was a promotion.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I'm going to turn now to the beginning of the conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And if we could have 65 ter 02559G.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, while it comes up, before the war Vlasenica was a multiethnic municipality; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, it was mainly Serb population, Muslim population, and a small percentage of Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you say in your statement that Vlasenica municipality was about evenly divided between Serbs and Muslims before the war?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If we could see page 2 of this document in the B/C/S only. This is an excerpt from the census.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And we see Vlasenica in line 1.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: We need to turn to page 3 now, still looking at the first line.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And looking on the left side, we see that as of 1991 Vlasenica had 33.942 people of whom 18.727 were Muslims, several thousand more than Serbs. So Vlasenica municipality had a Muslim majority before the war; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The interpreters couldn't hear you, sir. Could you please repeat your answer and try to speak into the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, according to this document the number of Muslims is higher.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'd tender this document, 02559G.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It's admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number, Mr. Registrar.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6870, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, between 1985 and the multiparty elections, ethnic relations in Vlasenica had been good; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part interethnic relations were good because this was a community that had a rather good economic status. There were quite a few profitable companies there, people were working, and - how do I put it? - no one bothered anyone else.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: The largest company in the municipality would have been Boksit Milici; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, inter alia, there were other companies that were profitable too.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now after the elections in 1990, relations between the different ethnic communities became polarised; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, this polarisation started happening more intensively when the establishment of political parties started, primarily the SDA. Later on the SDS was formed and then others, but these two were dominant in the area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Turning to the police station, after the multiparty elections it was the political parties, as you say in your statement I think, that appointed the professional staff in SJB Vlasenica. Now, you say in paragraph 4 that the person appointed chief after the elections was a Serb named Rade Bjelanovic. Mr. Bjelanovic was proposed by the SDS; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: His previous job had been at Boksit Milici and he had no law enforcement experience; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And can we go into private session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you meant --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Registrar. Mr. Djuric, we are at that time when we must take a break. We will -- can you please come back in 20 minutes. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We take a break and come back at ten to. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, I want to turn now to the Vlasenica SJB, and I'll start with some specific questions about the effect of the take-over of Vlasenica municipality on the SJB. Now, when the take-over happened, the non-Serb police officers at the Vlasenica SJB stopped working there; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Vlasenica Crisis Staff was formed on the 4th of April 1992. The SJB commander would attend meetings of that Crisis Staff; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the SJB would inform the civilian authorities of the municipality, either the Crisis Staff or War Presidency, about its work; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Formal reporting, however, went through the RS MUP's line of work; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, an individual report would be sent through the chain of command, wouldn't it?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And what that means is if you wanted to send information to the minister of the interior while you were chief of police, you would send it through the CSB?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, that was the way of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And as to the mechanics of that communication, beginning in June 1992 you had radio and teleprinter communication with CSB Sarajevo; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, communication had already been established. All relay station faced Tuzla and so on and so forth. So the services managed to establish a minimum of communication.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And once the teleprinter was up and running, you'd report on a daily basis to the CSB; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, dispatches could be drafted and dispatched.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And generally even before that teleprinter was working, the CSB was generally aware of what was going on at the Vlasenica SJB; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, but information never travelled fast. Before that it was sent by courier, and then new means were established so the information travelled faster by teleprinter or by phone.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I want to turn now to the special unit of the SJB. Now, you say in paragraph 29 of your statement that half of that special unit would be at the police station and the other half would be on leave and that they would work with the police at check-points and participate with the army in combat activities as needed. Is that all correct?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, they would receive their tasks at the police station; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, they were paid by the MUP and actually you signed the payrolls; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, they were on payroll at the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And you signed those payrolls?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, for the most part.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, could we have 65 ter 16972.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: This is a document dated the 10th of August, 1992, regarding disbanding of the special unit in the SJB. And you report: "Soon after the war started in the area of Vlasenica municipality (21 April 1992), a special purpose platoon was formed in the Vlasenica SJB in order to realise goals, and on the basis of agreement and suggestions of the Birac SAO government." That's the truth, what you're reporting to Mr. Cvijetic and the CSB here; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in the second paragraph here you say part of the unit became -- by the 10th of August and pursuant to this order by the minister of the interior at the end of July, part of it became a reserving contingent, part was transferred into the military police of the main command at Crna Rijeka, and part was given to the Serbian army. Now, "the Serbian army" means the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And the main command in Crna Rijeka, that's the Main Staff of the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, the Chamber has received evidence that Dragan Nikolic was one of the members of this unit. Was he given to the VRS at this point or did he become a reserve policeman?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: He first became a member of the TO and then the VRS. He did not stay long at the police station.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And just to be clear, you're aware that Mr. Nikolic pled guilty to certain crimes committed at Susica camp at this Tribunal; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, in your statement when you're discussing what was done with this special unit, you say some were sent to the army, some to Crna Rijeka, some to take a police course, and you also say: "... except for those who committed offences." Now, you don't say in this report to Mr. Cvijetic that any of the members of the unit were excepted from further service because they had committed further criminal offences, do you?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes, it is not mentioned in here; however, during the process to disband the unit, from the police station and from this unit, we sent away some 68 policemen for crimes and serious violation of work duties.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you'd sent a separate report about that a few days earlier to the Romanija Birac CSB; right? I can just --

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when I say "earlier," I mean a few days before this report; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say you sent people away for crimes, at that time what the police would do if a policeman was believed to have committed a crime was provide him to serve in the VRS; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: For the most part the rule was to remove such a person from our ranks and to file a criminal report against those individuals who had committed crimes, and we would hand them over to the VRS and then the VRS would go on to engage them in their units.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It is admitted. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit P6876, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we go into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are back in open session, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thanks. Yes, Mr. Traldi.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you've previously reviewed the Vlasenica crime register for 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, a majority of the cases that the Vlasenica SJB dealt with between April and July 1992 were cases involving possession of illegal weapons; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Now, you know from your previous review of the crime register that the people recorded there as having been arrested for illegal possession of weapons were all Muslims; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And when -- and when you looked -- when you did your -- when you did your review -- I'm afraid both of my microphones have stopped working.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: No, they haven't. You're fine.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Am I? Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you did your review of the log-book, you didn't see any registered reports against Serbs for crimes committed against non-Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: I am not aware of the structure of crimes, but there was a total of 125 crimes. I suppose that criminal reports were filed for at least some of those crimes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, I'm asking specifically of reports for crimes against non-Serbs committed by Serbs, and you didn't see any registered reports regarding such crimes, did you?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Correct. There was just one murder, a Serb killed another Serb and a criminal report was filed for that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: When you say there was just one, you refer to a Serb killing another Serb, were all 124 -- all of the other 124 reports against Muslims?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: No. I don't have the structure of those 128 crimes before, but those were various crimes, thefts, aggravated thefts, all sorts of violations of the law.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Well, could we have 65 ter 31509 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just before we do that, can I get back. You said no to the question whether all the other 124 reports were against Muslims. And then you said you don't have the structure of those crimes. Do we have to understand that in fact you do not know whether all 124 were Muslims?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know exactly. I think that that was not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Could we have 65 ter 31509, page 241.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And this will be part of one of the interviews that you had with the Tribunal as a suspect. So starting at the beginning of the page -- it's a very long interview so I'm afraid that we have we have only have it in English. I'll begin reading at line 13. "Let me ask you this: Did you file any criminal reports regarding crimes committed by Serbs against non-Serbs during this time-period? And you looked at the log-book, so perhaps that refreshed your memory. Did you file any crimes -- or criminal reports against Serbs?" And you responded: "I think I didn't see any registered reports." Now, does that refresh your recollection as to whether there were any registered reports in the log-book in Vlasenica in 1992 for crimes committed by Serbs against non-Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Stojanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am afraid that there is ambiguity. What is it that the Prosecutor is asking when he says "registered"?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Before you ask that question, can you tell us what is the -- [Microphone not activated].

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I beg your pardon. Before you ask that question, can you tell us what is the ambiguity that you are objecting to?

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would like to ask that you first see with the witness whether he speaks the English language, and then if he does not could he please be asked to take off his headphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Djuric, do you speak English at all? I saw you looking at the screen earlier.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's note: We cannot hear the witness. There is a lot background noise from different microphones.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can you answer my question? The interpreters didn't hear you, Mr. Djuric.

utterances.speaker: MR. STOJANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it won't work because my English is not good enough for me to address you in English, so I will just try to be clear enough. I do apologise. The question is vague because I think that the witness should be asked about the registers that are actually being referred to, where perpetrators of criminal acts are registered. There are different registers in the nomenclature in Bosnia-Herzegovina at that time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Well, as I understood the questions by the Prosecutor, there was no distinction made of different registers. The question was you reviewed your registers? Yes. You did not see any crimes committed by Serbs against non-Serbs - did not see - and in this interview he says yes he did not see. And he didn't ask for the log-book.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: If it's the term "registered reports" that Mr. Stojanovic is interested in, I can ask the witness to explain the significance of that. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi is making an offer which the Chamber will allow him to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, can you explain the significance of a registered report in the process of initiating and bringing criminal proceedings in SJB Vlasenica in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Here specifically, as far as I understand things, this is the situation: There is an internal book, the K registered in the crime prevention service, and then there is also a log-book at the prosecutor's office. And now the question is whether, as far as these records are concerned, the ones that you are dealing with, is it the records of the prosecutor's office or the public security station. Just that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And so when you said you didn't see any registered reports in the log-book you reviewed, which book would registered reports refer to?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: As far as I can remember, I think that what was shown to me was the prosecutor's office log-book, because all the crimes registered at the police station do not have to be included in the prosecutor's office book, so part of it is in the -- I mean, rather the number does not have to be the same of the crimes registered at the public security station and the crimes registered at the prosecutor's office. Usually there is less at the prosecutor's office.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honours, I see the time. I'd ask for two or three more questions on this topic just to close it for continuity.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, I also had some questions. Okay. You may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: At what stage -- well, let me actually try to make this very short. A person can't be convicted or judicially punished for a crime without the crime first having being registered in the prosecutor's log-book; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Did you say a person "can" or "can't," Mr. Traldi?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I said a person who can't, but let me make sure the witness understood.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: It is not possible for a person to be convicted or punished without the crime being in the prosecutor's log-book?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: So regardless of what investigations might have been done at the investigative stage by the police, it's correct that if the prosecutor's log-book contains no reports of crimes by Serbs against non-Serbs, no one was convicted or judicially punished for such a crime; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: And it's correct that when you reviewed that log-book, you saw no such reports; right?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Was that the prosecutor's log-book?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sorry, sir. Your answer wasn't recorded. It's correct that when you reviewed that log-book you saw no reports of crimes by Serbs against non-Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: That's right. If that's what I said then, then I think that's the way it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think you also had a couple of questions. That completes mine for the moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You have disposed of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: May I have just one final one for the day.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Sir, you said a moment ago that you would file criminal reports against police officers who were believed to have committed crimes. Clearly no police officers were convicted in Vlasenica for crimes against non-Serbs in 1992; right?

utterances.speaker: MANE DJURIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Traldi. Sir, we've come to the end of the day. We're going to break until tomorrow and we would like to see you tomorrow -- I beg your pardon, until Monday. Unfortunately, you still have to be re-examined by the Defence, so we'll see you on Monday morning at 9.30 in the morning. Is that right? Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now before you go, I just want to warn you that you may not speak or communicate with anybody whose -- whichever person it might be in connection with the testimony that you gave today or the testimony you still have to give on Monday, okay? Neither by writing or verbally. Is that understood?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Traldi, I take it you haven't concluded your cross-examination yet?

utterances.speaker: MR. TRALDI
utterances.text: I -- that was all I was going to say and to hope that the Chamber's interpretation that I was done for the moment as possibly meaning I was done was not a hopeful interpretation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The Chamber unreservedly withdraws that hopeful interpretation. Thank you so much. Okay. You'll still be cross-examined on Monday when we come back. You may follow the usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: We stand adjourned until Monday, the 3rd of November, at 9.30 in the morning in this very courtroom. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 3rd day of November, 2014, at 9.30 a.m. 25

procedural_notes.text: --- Whereupon the hearing adjourned at 2.23 p.m.,
